name: SK_Goblin_Soldier_PR

textures.channels: tangent normal, OpenGL (green up; flip green on import)
R occlusion, G roughness, B metallic

rig.rest_pose: standing pose as modelled (not a T pose)
rig.animation: none: skeleton and skin weights only; no clips, no Physics Asset, no control rig
rig.skeleton: bespoke (CONVENTIONS.md section 11: any skeleton with a single root bone named root)

pivot: feet: armature origin on the ground between the feet, front on -Y
dresses: goblin soldier, 1.37 m (2.0 m to the spike of his bill): olive warty skin, iron scale coat over breeches, crested helmet with a nasal, iron pauldrons, round wooden shield on the left arm, a broad-bladed bill in the right hand
status: source delivered; not imported into Unreal, not bound to any placement
known_weaknesses: NOT photoreal at 1 m. The body is a joint-graph sculpt (no modelled muscle, hands are mittens round the weapon, the face is pressed-in eyes and mouth with ball eyes and two tusks, no lids or nostrils). Garments are shells lifted off that body: real hems, but no seams, lacing or cloth simulation, and they bend with the automatic skin weights of the body. Helmet, weapon and shield are rigid on their bone; pauldrons are skinned. Decimated game mesh without joint loops. Clips are the poses made for the knight (clips_monsters.py). The horned goblin (Mog) is the same body in another kit, not a bigger build.
skeleton_note: bone names and hierarchy of the project humanoid core set (CONVENTIONS.md section 11), goblin proportions
